options.opa: The antibiotic oligomycin inhibits the passage of electrons through complex II.

enhanced_information: The antibiotic oligomycin inhibits the passage of electrons through complex II, also known as succinate dehydrogenase, which is part of the citric acid cycle. This inhibition affects energy production. Cytochromes are present in all respiratory complexes, with cytochrome C having a higher redox potential than cytochrome b in complex III.
analysis: In the transport of electrons through the respiratory chain, the antibiotic oligomycin inhibits the passage of electrons through complex II, also known as succinate dehydrogenase. The final reduction of O2 is actually produced by complex IV (cytochrome c oxidase), not the CoQ-cytochrome C reductase complex. FAD-dependent dehydrogenases interact with the succinate CoQ reductase complex. Cytochromes are present in all respiratory complexes, but the order of redox potential varies, with cytochrome C having a higher redox potential than cytochrome b in complex III.
